activity.notes: Sargon of Akkad was the founding king of the Akkadian dynasty and established a territorial empire centered on Akkad/Agade after conquering the Sumerian city-states. ATLAS uses the widely cited 2334-2279 BCE reign convention as a representative chronology, but both endpoints are approximate because third-millennium BCE Mesopotamian absolute chronology is reconstructed and major scholarly references use alternative placements, including ca. 2340-2285 BCE. The user-supplied civilization label Akkad is normalized to the map-level historical polity Akkadian Empire rather than treated as only the city of Akkad.

sources.title: Akkadian — Collections Online, British Museum
sources.citation_text: The British Museum identifies Sargon I as the first king of the Akkadian Dynasty, states that he united the whole of Mesopotamia under one ruler, and dates the dynasty beginning to 2334 BCE.

sources.title: The Akkadian Period (ca. 2350–2150 B.C.) — The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.citation_text: The Metropolitan Museum identifies Sargon as the first king of the dynasty and dates his reign approximately 2340-2285 BCE, documenting the chronological variation that requires approximate ATLAS boundaries.

sources.title: Fragment d'une stèle de victoire d'un roi d'Akkad — Louvre Collections
sources.citation_text: The Louvre catalogs an Akkadian victory-stele fragment under the period of Sargon of Akkad and gives the Sargonic date range 2334-2279 BCE, supporting the conventional chronology used for the ATLAS representative interval.

sources.title: 사르곤 — 한국가톨릭대사전
sources.citation_text: The Korean encyclopedia uses the form 아카드의 사르곤 and gives 2334-2279 BCE, supporting the Korean display name and the representative conventional chronology.
